title: How to Convert Your Property Valuer Salary from Hourly to Annual

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

Understanding your annual pay from an hourly rate is straightforward. Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and other deductions. For full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work a different number of hours, adjust accordingly.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00 and you work 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Your fortnightly pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 2 = $2,280 before tax. This simple formula assumes you receive the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

## Property Valuer Salary Under the Real Estate Industry Award

Property valuers in Australia are often classified under the Real Estate Industry Award 2020. According to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide for that award, minimum rates apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. For a full-time adult employee, the hourly rates are:

- Level 1 (associate) – first 12 months: $26.59 per hour
- Level 1 (associate) – after 12 months: $28.00 per hour
- Level 2 (representative): $29.45 per hour
- Level 3 (supervisory): $32.39 per hour
- Level 4 (in-charge): $33.88 per hour

These rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, which applies to award-free employees. A property valuer salary at Level 2, for instance, would be $29.45 per hour, or $1,119.10 per week. Using the conversion formula, the annual gross pay at Level 2 is $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,173 per year.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual property valuer, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is paid on top of the base rate, not a combined figure. For a casual employee at Level 2, the hourly rate becomes $29.45 × 1.25 = $36.81 per hour. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; always start with the base hourly rate and add the loading separately. The super guarantee requires your employer to pay an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings into your super fund, on top of your gross pay. For the 2026–27 year, this applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,000. For a property valuer salary at Level 2, the super contribution would be about $6,981 per year, paid in addition to your gross pay. This is an estimate based on ordinary earnings only.

## Tax Considerations

Your annual gross pay from your property valuer salary is subject to Australian resident tax rates for 2026–27. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income from $18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15%, $45,001 to $135,000 at 30%, $135,001 to $190,000 at 37%, and above $190,000 at 45%. The Medicare levy of 2% also applies. For a full-time property valuer earning $58,173 per year, the estimated tax and Medicare would be about $9,000, leaving a take-home pay of around $49,000. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed estimate.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual gross pay, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It uses the Fair Work Commission’s 38-hour week and the ATO’s 2026–27 tax scales. Remember that this is an estimate – it does not include penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or the Medicare levy surcharge. For award-specific rates, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

## Distinguishing Minimum and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates, such as those for property valuers, are higher. The Fair Work Commission sets these rates annually. Always check the correct award for your classification. The Real Estate Industry Award covers many property valuers, but some may fall under the Professional Employees Award. Use our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide to find your classification.

## Final Thoughts

Converting your property valuer salary from hourly to annual is simple with the formula hourly × hours per week × 52. For full-time work, assume 38 hours. Your fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2. Remember that super is paid on top, and tax is deducted from your gross pay. Use our tools to get a personalised estimate.
